===Etymology 1===
{{wikidata lexeme|L784}}
From {{inh|en|enm|questioun}}, from {{der|en|xno|questiun}}, from {{der|en|fro|question}}, from {{der|en|la|quaestiōnem}}, accusative of {{m|la|quaestiō||a seeking, investigation, inquiry, question}}, from {{m|la|quaerere||to seek, ask, inquire}},<ref name="Cent1911">{{R:Century}}</ref> of uncertain origin, but possibly from {{der|en|itc-pro|*kʷaizeō}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*kʷeh₂-||to acquire}}. {{doublet|en|quest}}.

Partially displaced native {{ncog|ang|āscung}}, whence [[asking]]. Compare also {{cog|gml|quēstie|t=questioning; inquiry}}, {{cog|gmh|questje|t=question}}.

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# A [[worded]] or [[expressed]] [[sentence]], [[phrase]], or only a [[word]] on its own, [[which]] [[asks]] [[for]] [[information]], a [[reply]], or a [[response]]; an [[interrogative]].
#: {{syn|en|inquiry|enquiry|query|[[interrogation]] (''formal'')}}
#: {{ux|en|What is your '''question'''?}}
#* {{RQ:Lincoln Pratt's Patients|chapter=4|passage=I told him about everything I could think of; and what I couldn't think of he did. He asked about six '''questions''' during my yarn, but every '''question''' had a point to it. At the end he bowed and thanked me once more. As a thanker he was main-truck high; I never see anybody so polite.}}
#* {{quote-av|en|date=2006 Feb 3|writer=w:Graham Linehan|title=w:The IT Crowd|season=1|number=4
|text=Can I ask you two a '''question'''? / Please, [[Christ]], yes. / How can you two live like this? / How can... / Don't [[google]] the '''question''', Moss!}}
#* {{RQ:Time|title=Can I Ask Someone if They’re on Ozempic?|author=Angela Haupt|date=Jan 29 2026
|text=When bodies change quickly or noticeably, assumptions often follow—and so does the desire to ask one potentially fraught '''question''': Did medication play a role?
|url=https://time.com/7358259/asking-about-ozempic-body-talk/
|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260201212757/https://time.com/7358259/asking-about-ozempic-body-talk/}}
# A [[subject]] or [[topic]] for [[consideration]] or [[investigation]].
#: {{syn|en|subject|topic|problem|consideration|proposition}}
#: {{ux|en|The '''question''' of seniority will be discussed at the meeting.}}
#: {{ux|en|There was a '''question''' of which material to use.}}
#: {{ux|en|I've ordered it all, but there’s still the '''question''' of who’s going to pay.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=14 October 2014 |author=David Malcolm|page=173|title=The Great War Re-Remembered: Allohistory and Allohistorical Fiction|work=The Great War in Post-Memory Literature and Film|editors=Martin Löschnigg; Marzena Sokolowska-Paryz |url= https://books.google.co.nz/books?id=4Y_nBQAAQBAJ |publisher={{w|de Gruyter|Walter de Gruyter GmbH & Co KG.}}|isbn= 9783110363029 |passage= The '''question''' of the plausibility of the counter-factual is seen as key in all three discussions of allohistorical fiction (as it is in Demandt's and Ferguson's examinations of allohistory) (cf. Rodiek 25–26; Ritter 15–16; Helbig 32).}}
# A doubt or [[challenge]] about the truth, accuracy{{,}} or validity of a matter.
#: {{syn|en|issue|doubt}}
#: {{ux|en|His claim to the property has come under '''question'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|The story is true beyond '''question'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|He obeyed without '''question'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|There was no '''question''' of his blaming me for his frustration.}}
#* {{RQ:King James Version|John|3|25|passage=There arose a '''question''' between some of John's disciples and the Jews about purifying.}}
#* {{RQ:Bacon Holy War|passage=It is to be to '''question''', whether it be lawful for Christian princes or states to make an invasive war, only and simply for the propagation of the faith.}}
#* {{RQ:Time|author=Ciara Nugent|title=Can Public Transit Survive the Pandemic? London's New Transport Commissioner Wants You to Believe It Can|date=April 2 2021|passage=The pandemic has not only caused an immediate fall in ticket revenues for the world’s public transit networks—rail ridership in Barcelona, Moscow, Beijing and New York City at times plummeting 80%—in some cities it also has thrown into '''question''' the future of mass urban transportation.|url=https://time.com/5951769/andy-byford-mta-tfl-interview/|accessdate=6 April 2021|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20210403170844/https://time.com/5951769/andy-byford-mta-tfl-interview/|archivedate=3 April 2021}}
# A [[proposal]] to a [[meeting]] as a [[topic]] for [[deliberation]].
#: {{syn|en|proposal}}
#: {{ux|en|I move that the '''question''' be put to a vote.}}
# {{lb|en|now|archaic|historical|chiefly|with definite article}} [[interrogation|Interrogation]] by [[torture]].
#* {{RQ:Smollett Peregrine Pickle|volume=II|chapter=LXXVII|passage=I, not at all ambitious of the crown of martyrdom, resolved to temporize: so that, when I was brought to the '''question''' the second time, I made a solemn recantation {{...}}}}
#* {{RQ:Macaulay History of England|chapter=2|passage=The Scottish privy council had power to put state prisoners to the '''question'''.}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} [[talk|Talk]]; [[conversation]]; [[speech]].
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare King Lear|act=IV|scene=iii|passage=Made she no verbal '''question'''?}}

===Etymology 2===
{{wikidata lexeme|L48}}
From {{inh|en|enm|questionen}}, {{m|enm|questyonen}}, partly from {{der|en|frm|questionner}} and partly from the noun.<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=v|id=7829390065}}</ref><ref>{{R:MED Online|entry=questiǒunen|pos=v|id=MED35583}}</ref>

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To ask questions of; to [[interrogate]]; to [[ask]] for information.
#: {{syn|en|query}}
#* {{quote-book|en|title=East and West|passage=Yet he lingered in Perryville with the determination of seeing Ruth, and '''questioning''' her about Helen Murray's letters.|year=1836|author=Frederick W. Thomas|volume=2}}
#* {{quote-av|en|title=True Detective|text=Another former resident noticed the car because it was new and upscale and no one ever came back to '''question''' him. This points to serious flaws in the investigation from the beginning.|year=2019|author=Nic Pizzolatto|medium=television|season=3|number=4|episode=The Hour and the Day}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To raise {{l|en|doubt|doubts}} about; have doubts about.
#: {{syn|en|query|contest}}
#* {{quote-av
|en
|date=4/17/1985
|author=w:Frank Herbert
|title=Frank Herbert speaking at UCLA 4/17/1985
|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170210174612/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5IfgBX1EW00
|archivedate=10 February 2017
|publisher=UCLACommStudies
|time=15:46
|text='''Question''' things. I have the most fun when I'm writing '''questioning''' things that people do not '''question'''- the assumptions that everybody knows are true.}}
#* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Paul Glader|title=Four takeaways from Walter Isaacson’s biography of Elon Musk|url=https://www.cnn.com/2023/09/12/tech/elon-musk-isaacson-biography-takeaways/index.html|date=2023-09-12|passage=Isaacson reports that Musk’s fractured relationship with Jenna, who is trans, partly led to Musk’s rightward turn toward libertarianism and '''questioning''' what he considers the “woke-mind-virus, which is fundamentally antiscience, antimerit, and antihuman.”|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260412195435/https://www.cnn.com/2023/09/12/tech/elon-musk-isaacson-biography-takeaways/index.html|archivedate=12 April 2026}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To ask a question or questions; inquire or seek to know; examine.<ref name="Cent1911"/>
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1597|author=w:Francis Bacon|title=[[s:The Works of Francis Bacon, Volume 1/Essays/Of Discourse|Of Discourse]]
|passage=He that '''questioneth''' much shall learn much.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive|obsolete}} To argue; to converse; to dispute.
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Merchant of Venice|IV|i|passage=I pray you, think you '''question''' with the Jew.}}
